resources.title: Physics equation sheet
resources.summary: All 35 equations on AQA's Physics equation sheet, grouped by topic, with what every symbol stands for and its unit. The six marked HT are for Higher tier papers only.
resources.statusNote: Follows AQA's sheet for June 2027, which prints all 35. Ofqual's decision of 5 May 2026 keeps the sheet, unchanged, for exams from 2028, as the equations students must be able to use and apply but are "not required to memorise"; AQA publishes each year's by 1 September of the year before. No question will ask you just to copy one down: the marks are for choosing the right equation, rearranging it and using the units.

sources.name: Ofqual: formulae and equation sheets from 2028

applications.title: Car crash safety
applications.body: Crumple zones and airbags make the stop take longer. With $F = \dfrac{m\,\Delta v}{\Delta t}$, the same change in momentum over a longer time means a smaller force on the passenger.

applications.title: Your electricity bill
applications.body: A 2 kW kettle running for a quarter of an hour uses $E = P\,t = 2 \times 0.25 = 0.5$ kWh. The bill is that number times the price per kilowatt-hour.

applications.title: Wi-Fi and radio
applications.body: A 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi signal travels at $3 \times 10^8$ m/s, so $\lambda = \dfrac{v}{f} = 0.125$ m: about 12.5 cm, which sets the size of the aerial inside a router.

applications.title: Charging a phone
applications.body: A phone charger is a transformer. It steps 230 V mains down to about 5 V, so its coils have roughly 46 times as many turns on the primary as on the secondary.

items.name: Elastic potential energy
items.symbols: $k$ spring constant (N/m), $e$ extension (m). Only while the limit of proportionality is not exceeded.

items.name: Efficiency from energy
items.symbols: A fraction or a percentage, with no unit. The sheet says "useful output energy transfer" over "total input energy transfer".

items.name: Efficiency from power
items.symbols: No unit. Never more than 1, or 100%.

items.name: Power from current and resistance
items.symbols: Square the current first, then multiply.

items.name: Change of state
items.symbols: $L$ specific latent heat (J/kg). No temperature change: the energy breaks or makes bonds.

items.name: Gas pressure and volume
items.symbols: $p$ pressure (Pa), $V$ volume (m³). For a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, so $p_1V_1 = p_2V_2$.

items.name: Work done
items.symbols: $W$ work done (J), $F$ force (N), $s$ distance along the line of the force (m)

items.name: Moment
items.symbols: $M$ moment (N m), $d$ perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of the force (m)

items.name: Pressure
items.symbols: $p$ pressure (Pa), $F$ force at right angles to the surface (N), $A$ area (m²)

items.name: Pressure in a liquid
items.symbols: $h$ height of the column (m), $\rho$ density of the liquid (kg/m³)

items.name: Force and change in momentum
items.symbols: $m\,\Delta v$ change in momentum (kg m/s), $\Delta t$ time taken (s)

items.name: Magnification
items.symbols: A ratio, so no unit. Physics only, with lenses.

items.name: Force on a conductor
items.symbols: $B$ magnetic flux density (T), $I$ current (A), $l$ length in the field (m). At right angles to the field.

items.name: Transformer turns
items.symbols: $V$ potential difference (V), $n$ number of turns, $p$ primary coil, $s$ secondary coil

items.name: Transformer power
items.symbols: Power in equals power out, for a transformer that is 100% efficient.

resources.title: SI units and prefixes
resources.summary: The unit every quantity on the equation sheet is measured in, and the prefixes from nano to tera, with how to convert between them.

applications.title: Reading a plug-in charger
applications.body: A charger labelled 5 V, 2000 mA gives $2000 \times 10^{-3} = 2$ A, so its power is $P = V\,I = 10$ W.

applications.title: Light and the size of atoms
applications.body: Green light has a wavelength of about 500 nm, $5 \times 10^{-7}$ m. An atom is about $10^{-10}$ m across, five thousand times smaller.

applications.title: Power stations
applications.body: A large power station is rated at about 2 GW, which is $2 \times 10^9$ W. That would run a million 2 kW kettles at once: $\dfrac{2 \times 10^9}{2 \times 10^3} = 10^6$.

blocks.title: Quantities and their units
blocks.note: Mass is in kilograms, not grams, and time in seconds, not minutes or hours: convert before you substitute.

blocks.title: Prefixes
blocks.note: To go from a prefixed unit to the base unit, multiply by the power of ten. To go back, divide. A kilowatt-hour is energy, not power: $1$ kWh $= 1000$ W $\times 3600$ s $= 3\,600\,000$ J.

resources.title: Circuit symbols
resources.summary: The fourteen circuit symbols AQA lists, each drawn and labelled with what the component does, coloured by family: power, switches, meters, resistors, and parts that light up or work one way.

applications.title: Reading a wiring diagram
applications.body: Electricians and engineers draw every circuit, from a doorbell to a car, in these same symbols, so a diagram drawn in one country can be built in another.

applications.title: Automatic street lights
applications.body: A street light that switches on at dusk uses an LDR: as the light fades its resistance rises, and the circuit uses that change to turn the lamp on.

applications.title: Thermostats and fire alarms
applications.body: A thermistor’s resistance falls as it warms, so a heating controller or a heat alarm reads the temperature from the current through it.

visual.alt: Fourteen circuit symbols on tiles in two columns: cell, battery, open and closed switch, fuse, ammeter, voltmeter, resistor, variable resistor, thermistor, LDR, lamp, diode and LED, each named with what it does and coloured by family

blocks.body: **Drawing them in the exam.** Use a ruler for the wires and join them at right angles. An ammeter goes **in series**, in the loop itself; a voltmeter goes **in parallel**, across the component it measures. The long line of a cell is its **positive** side.

resources.title: Electromagnetic spectrum
resources.summary: The seven groups of electromagnetic waves in order, from radio waves to gamma rays, with the uses the specification lists for each and the harm the three most energetic can do.

applications.title: Your phone uses three of them
applications.body: It talks to the mast with radio waves and microwaves, and its camera records visible light. The same phone’s face unlock often shines infrared at you.

applications.title: Hospitals
applications.body: X-rays pass through soft tissue but not bone, which is how an X-ray image shows a fracture. Gamma rays from a carefully aimed source destroy cancer cells in radiotherapy.

applications.title: Sun cream
applications.body: The SPF on a bottle measures protection from ultraviolet, the part of sunlight that ages skin and raises the risk of skin cancer.

visual.alt: The electromagnetic spectrum as seven rows from radio waves at the top to gamma rays at the bottom, each with a wave drawn shorter than the last, its typical wavelength, its uses, and for ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays the harm they can do

blocks.body: **Remember the order.** A common mnemonic is *Rich Men In Vegas Use eXpensive Gadgets*: radio, microwaves, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma. All seven travel at the same speed in a vacuum, $3 \times 10^8$ m/s, so by $v = f\lambda$ a shorter wavelength means a higher frequency.

resources.title: Required practicals
resources.summary: The ten required practicals in AQA Physics: what each investigates, what you change and what you measure. Two are Physics only, not in Combined Science.

blocks.title: The ten required practicals
rows: the energy supplied, by heating for longer
the temperature rise of a block of known mass; then $c = \dfrac{\Delta E}{m\,\Delta\theta}$
the insulating material, or its thickness
how fast a beaker of hot water cools
the length of a wire; resistors in series and in parallel
the current and the pd; then $R = \dfrac{V}{I}$
the pd across a filament lamp, a diode and a resistor
the current through each, to plot an I–V graph
regular solids, irregular solids and liquids
mass on a balance, and volume from dimensions or by displacement
the force on a spring, by adding masses
the extension, from the spring’s original length
the force at constant mass, then the mass at constant force
waves in a ripple tank and in a solid
the surface, or the substance the light enters
the angles of incidence, reflection and refraction
the kind of surface: matt or shiny, black or white
how much infrared it gives out or absorbs
blocks.note: AQA says questions drawing on these count for at least 15% of the marks, each on the paper that covers its topic. Know the method, the variables and what could go wrong with each.

applications.title: Choosing loft insulation
applications.body: Practical 2 is how a manufacturer compares insulating materials: the one that lets hot water cool slowest keeps a house warm for the least money.

applications.title: Crash testing
applications.body: Practical 7 is Newton’s second law measured. Car makers measure the acceleration of a crash dummy in exactly this way to find the force on a passenger.
